paragraphs.source_en: It was already noon when Hidetada heard the gunfire at Tennōji and gave the order to commence battle. Until then, Hidetada had faithfully heeded his father's warning not to advance rashly and intended to keep watching the situation.

paragraphs.source_en: Had Mōri Katsunaga, who had fought his way forward, not appeared before his lines, Shogun Hidetada might have delayed the order to engage still longer. It was the hour for the midday meal, he thought, and his two young brothers, still strangers to battle, must now be opening their ration bags behind their father... Yet Mōri's furious charge across the field became the spark that set the great battle ablaze.

paragraphs.source_en: Honda Masashige's unit, the Maeda vanguard, hurried forward along the eastern line. units.source_en: Honda Masashige's unit, the Maeda vanguard, hurried forward along the eastern line. paragraphs.source_en: The first to leave the Kantō camp would be Date Masamune, followed by Maeda Toshitsune, Asano Nagaakira, and the others. How could they willingly remain beneath the shogunate Tokugawa Ieyasu had created for the sake of peace? Like Sanada Yukimura, they would surely seek freedom anew. Whether Kuroda Nagamasa, who had once saved Hidetada, or Katō Yoshiaki and Katagiri Katsumoto, all would become wild horses that had slipped their reins. To divide the Kantō armies was Yukimura's greatest purpose in this battle.
